subsystems.name: Exotic-matter shell
subsystems.role: the layer of negative energy density that contracts space ahead of the craft and expands it behind, creating the bubble.

subsystems.name: Metric control system
subsystems.role: adjusts the shape and strength of the bubble so the craft can accelerate, coast and stop.

subsystems.name: Crew compartment
subsystems.role: a region of ordinary, flat space-time inside the bubble where tidal forces and radiation stay survivable.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: supplies whatever it takes to generate and hold the negative energy configuration.
parts: not specified — no known source is remotely sufficient

subsystems.name: Navigation
subsystems.role: aims the bubble at a target and, in principle, steers it.

subsystems.name: Bubble termination
subsystems.role: collapses the bubble at the destination without releasing its stored energy destructively.

buildSteps.title: Derive a workable metric
buildSteps.detail: Solve the equations of general relativity for a bubble geometry whose energy requirements are physically plausible, rather than the original 1994 Alcubierre solution, which demanded more negative energy than exists in the observable universe.

buildSteps.title: Show the energy can actually exist
buildSteps.detail: Demonstrate that a source of negative energy density can be produced in the required quantity and held in place. The Casimir effect shows negative energy density is real, but only in concentrations around 10⁻¹⁵ m and vanishingly small totals.

buildSteps.title: Satisfy the quantum inequalities
buildSteps.detail: Prove the configuration does not violate the limits physics places on how much negative energy can persist in one place for how long; published analyses of the original design do violate them.

buildSteps.title: Solve the horizon problem
buildSteps.detail: Inside the original bubble there is a causal horizon, so no signal can reach the front edge to switch the drive off. A usable design needs a geometry without that horizon.

buildSteps.title: Build the shell
buildSteps.detail: In theory, assemble a torus or shell of field-generating elements around the craft, capable of imposing the required stress-energy distribution on the surrounding space-time.

buildSteps.title: Establish the interior
buildSteps.detail: Create and verify the flat-space region inside, checking tidal forces and particle production at the bubble walls — accelerating boundaries are predicted to radiate.

buildSteps.title: Test at small scale
buildSteps.detail: Demonstrate a measurable, microscopic distortion of space-time that can be switched on and off, then scale it. No experiment of this kind has been proposed that is within reach of current technology.

buildSteps.title: Pilot the craft
buildSteps.detail: Only after all of the above: enclose a crew, form the bubble, travel, and collapse it at the destination.
